transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. I know it doesn’t make sense, but the thought of going into any kind of medical office or having tests done scares me so much that I keep putting off appointments I really need. It's gotten to the point where I'm avoiding things that are actually quite important.
Do you mainly fear being in medical settings because you might be judged or embarrassed, or is it more the possibility of needles, blood, tests, or other medical procedures themselves?

Oh, it’s not about being judged or embarrassed at all. It is specifically the medical environments themselves, like walking into a clinic or having to lie in an imaging machine like an MRI. The thought of the actual procedures and tests is what completely overwhelms me.
When you face a medical setting or procedure, do you get sudden panic symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, dizziness, or feeling like you might faint?

Yes, absolutely. Even just getting a reminder text or seeing a medical scene on TV makes my heart pound, my hands sweat, and gives me this overwhelming urge to escape. When I actually try to go to an appointment, I end up sitting in the parking lot shaking and crying in my car.
Do you fear only medical procedures and settings, or do you also have the same intense fear in other situations such as heights, flying, enclosed spaces, or animals?

No, it's really just medical environments and procedures. I don't have any issues with heights, flying, or animals at all. This intense dread is strictly limited to things like doctors' offices, clinics, and medical tests.
Have you ever had a specific traumatic or very painful medical experience, such as a bad injection, blood draw, or procedure, that started this fear?

No, I haven't had a botched procedure or anything like that, but this intense fear really started about thirteen months ago when I slipped on some ice, fractured my wrist, and had to go to the ER. I always had a mild discomfort with hospitals before then, but that visit crystallized everything into the dread I feel now.
When you feel this fear, is it mainly triggered by seeing blood, injections, or injuries, or is it more the medical settings and procedures themselves like clinics, exams, or MRI machines?

It is definitely the medical settings and procedures themselves, rather than blood or needles. Just walking into a doctor's office or thinking about being put in an MRI machine makes my stomach drop and my anxiety spike. It's the whole environment and the tests that terrify me, not injections or injuries.
Do you also have a strong fear of being outside your home or in places where it would be hard to get help if you felt panicky, or is the fear limited only to medical settings and procedures?

No, I don't have any fear of being outside my home or in public places at all. This intense dread is strictly limited to medical settings, clinics, and procedures. I am perfectly fine going anywhere else, but the moment it involves a doctor's office or a medical test, the panic sets in.
When you think about medical settings, is the fear mainly about becoming trapped or unable to escape, or is it more a fear of the medical procedures themselves even if you could leave at any time?

It is definitely more about the medical procedures and the environments themselves, rather than a fear of being trapped. While the anxiety does make me feel a strong urge to escape, the actual dread is entirely focused on what might happen during the appointments or being inside those medical machines.
Do you fear only medical settings and procedures, or do you also have a similar strong fear of other specific things like injections, blood, injuries, or seeing medical images?

It really is just the medical settings and tests themselves, like being in an MRI machine, rather than blood or injuries. I do get panicked even just seeing those medical procedures or machines on TV, though. But the core of my dread is physically being in those offices and having to undergo the tests.

When you think about medical appointments, is your fear mainly about the procedure itself being dangerous or harmful, or is it more a general fear of medical environments and tests even when you know they are safe?

It's definitely more of a general, irrational dread of the medical environments and the machines themselves. Even though I logically know that these routine tests and check-ups are safe, just the thought of being in those settings makes my stomach drop. My mind immediately jumps to worst-case scenarios, even though I know it doesn't make sense.
Do you fear only medical settings and procedures, or do you also have a strong fear of being alone outside your home or in places where it would be hard to get help if you panicked?

No, I don't have any fear of being alone outside or in public places at all. I can go anywhere else without feeling anxious, as long as it doesn't involve medical care. This dread is strictly limited to doctors' offices, clinics, and medical tests.
Do you fear all medical settings and procedures in general, or is the fear mainly tied to one specific thing like injections, blood draws, dental work, or imaging machines?

It has actually become quite general. While it started as a minor discomfort, it has grown into a dread of walking into almost any medical setting, especially doctors' offices, clinics, and imaging suites. It isn't limited to just one specific thing like needles; it is the entire environment and the tests themselves that terrify me.
Is your fear mainly about one specific medical trigger, like needles or blood, or does it happen with almost any medical setting or test, such as clinics, exams, and imaging machines?

It is definitely not about a single trigger like needles or blood, but rather about almost any medical setting, exam, or imaging machine like an MRI. Even just walking into a clinic or thinking about lying in one of those machines triggers intense anxiety for me. It makes my stomach drop and my mind immediately jump to worst-case scenarios.
Do you also have a strong fear of one specific medical trigger, like needles, blood, or injections, or is it mainly the broader medical settings and tests themselves?

It is definitely the broader medical settings and tests themselves, rather than specific triggers like needles or blood. Just the thought of walking into a clinic or having to lie inside one of those MRI machines is what triggers my intense anxiety.
Do you also feel this same intense fear with other specific medical triggers like needles, blood draws, or injections, or is it mainly the broader medical settings and tests themselves?

I'm not entirely sure how I would feel about specific things like needles or blood draws, as I haven't had to face them recently. My main dread is definitely focused on the broader medical settings, like walking into clinics and having to use those imaging machines. That is what truly terrifies me.
Have you ever had a strong fear or panic response specifically to needles, blood draws, or injections, or is your fear mainly limited to medical settings and tests like clinics and MRI machines?

No, I’ve never had that kind of intense panic response to needles or blood draws specifically. While nobody particularly likes getting a shot, they don't trigger the severe dread and avoidance that walking into a clinic or facing an MRI machine does. My fear is definitely focused on the medical environments and the tests themselves.

Do you ever get this same intense fear in other situations where you have to be in a medical-like enclosed space, such as a dentist’s office or a treatment room, or is it only with doctors’ offices, clinics, and imaging tests like MRI?

I’m not entirely sure about the dentist since I haven't been recently, but it is definitely medical clinics, doctors' suites, and scanning machines that trigger my intense anxiety. Those are the specific places connected to my fall and my back pain referrals. Just the thought of going into those environments is what makes my stomach drop and causes me to avoid them.

Do you also get this intense fear in other medical situations like dental visits, blood tests, or minor procedures, or is it mainly limited to clinics, doctors' offices, and imaging machines such as MRI scans?

Yes, the dread is actually quite broad and covers almost any medical office, test, or procedure, including things like blood tests. While my most recent and severe struggles have been with the clinics and imaging machines recommended for my back, the fear applies to almost any medical setting. I would feel that same intense anxiety facing any of those other procedures as well.

Do you fear only medical settings and procedures, or do you also have this same intense fear in one specific medical situation, like injections, blood draws, or seeing blood? This will help me tell whether the fear is broad and general or tied to a more specific trigger.

It is definitely broader and centered on medical environments in general, like walking into clinics or having to lie in an MRI machine. I don't have a specific fear of blood or needles, but rather the intense dread of being in those medical settings and undergoing scans or exams.

Do you fear only medical settings and procedures, or do you also have a strong fear of one specific trigger like blood, needles, or injections? This will help me tell whether this is a broad medical-environment phobia or a more specific one.

It is definitely the medical environments and procedures themselves that I fear, rather than blood or needles. Just the thought of walking into a clinic or being inside an imaging machine like an MRI is what triggers my anxiety. It's the whole setting and the tests that I dread, not specific things like injections.
Do you fear all medical settings and procedures in general, or is there one specific trigger such as injections, blood draws, or seeing blood that causes the strongest fear?

It is definitely the general medical settings and diagnostic tests rather than needles, blood, or injections. Walking into any clinic or the thought of being in an imaging machine is what really triggers my anxiety. I don't have a specific fear of blood or shots at all.

When you think about going to a medical appointment, is your main fear that you will be trapped or unable to escape, or is it more the medical procedures and environment themselves even if you could leave at any time?

My fear is definitely about the medical procedures and the environment itself rather than being trapped. Although I feel a strong urge to escape when the panic sets in, the real dread is focused on the clinic setting and the tests themselves.
Is your fear mainly of the medical setting and procedures themselves, or is it specifically triggered by blood, injections, or seeing injuries?

It is definitely the medical settings and the procedures themselves that terrify me, not blood, injections, or injuries. Just the thought of walking into a clinic or having to do a diagnostic test is what triggers this intense dread and anxiety.

When you picture the feared medical situation, is the worst part the chance of seeing blood, needles, or injuries, or is it the medical environment and procedures themselves even without those things?

It is definitely the medical environment and the procedures themselves, even if there are no needles or blood involved at all. Just the thought of walking into a clinic or having to lie in an imaging machine is what triggers my anxiety and makes my stomach drop.
Do you ever have this same intense fear in situations involving blood, needles, or injections, or is it limited to medical settings and procedures like clinics and MRI scans?

No, I don't really have that fear with blood or needles on their own. While the thought of invasive tests in those settings does worry me, the intense dread and panic are really triggered by the thought of physically going into the clinics, offices, or getting into those scanning machines. It is the environments themselves that terrify me.

Do you have this same intense fear with any one specific medical trigger, such as blood draws, injections, or seeing blood, or is it mainly the broader fear of medical offices, exams, and imaging machines themselves?

It is definitely the broader fear of the medical offices and imaging machines themselves, rather than blood or needles. Just the thought of walking into a clinic, or even seeing an MRI machine on a TV show, is enough to trigger my intense anxiety.
Do you also have this same intense fear with blood, injections, or seeing injuries, or is it mainly limited to medical offices, exams, and imaging machines like MRI?

No, I don't have that intense fear with blood, injections, or injuries at all. It is strictly limited to the medical environments like clinics, offices, and those imaging machines. The clinical setting itself and the thought of being in those machines are what trigger my anxiety.

Do you also feel this intense fear in other enclosed medical-like situations, such as being in a dental chair or a treatment room, or is it limited to clinics, doctor’s offices, and imaging machines like MRI?

Yes, my fear is heavily focused on doctors' offices, clinics, and imaging suites like MRIs, and walking into any clinical treatment room or medical environment makes my stomach drop. I haven't had to deal with any dental appointments recently, so my anxiety is entirely consumed by the medical appointments and spinal tests I've been avoiding.
Do you also fear or avoid blood draws, injections, or seeing blood, or is your anxiety mainly about medical offices, exams, and imaging machines like MRI scans?

My anxiety is definitely focused on the medical offices, exams, and imaging machines rather than blood draws or injections. While invasive tests in general worry me, the intense panic and avoidance are triggered by the thought of walking into a clinic, sitting in the waiting room, or being put into those scanning machines.
Do you also get the same intense fear with blood, injections, or seeing injuries, or is it mainly the broader fear of medical offices, exams, and imaging machines themselves?

No, I don't have that intense fear with blood, injections, or injuries. It is definitely the broader medical settings, like walking into a clinic or lying in an MRI machine, that terrify me. Just thinking about being in those environments makes my heart pound and gives me an overwhelming urge to escape.
